page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.24xlarge is an accelerated compute instance within the ecs.gn6e family, built on KVM virtualization to support high-density parallel compute tasks. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor offering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, FMA, BMI2, and AES cryptography.

Acceleration is anchored by eight NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs, each equipped with 32 GB of VRAM for an aggregate GPU memory footprint of 256 GB. Host memory capacity is 736 GB, resulting in approximately 7.67 GB of system RAM per vCPU. Networking interfaces provide a 32 Gbps baseline throughput. The instance includes no integrated local storage, meaning input datasets and scratch storage must be provisioned via attached network block storage.

Benchmark data reflects the architectural tradeoffs of the multi-socket Intel Xeon configuration. In stress-ng evaluations, single-core CPU performance falls within the bottom 25 percent with a score of 1104.49, reflecting conservative base clock speeds. Conversely, multi-core scaling reaches 70674.73 in stress-ng, placing aggregate CPU throughput in the top 25 percent. The hardware configuration emphasizes dense GPU compute and system memory density rather than single-threaded CPU speed or integrated NVMe storage. Workloads aligned with this server profile include multi-GPU deep learning training, seismic data processing, large-scale scientific simulations, and parallel rendering pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for distributed training, high-performance computing, and parallel data processing. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support. Hardware acceleration is provided by 8 NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs, offering a combined 256 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM with 32 GB per GPU. System memory totals 736 GB, establishing an allocation of 7.67 GB per vCPU core. Network performance is anchored by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data. In synthetic testing, single-core CPU throughput registers in the lower quartile, whereas the 96 dedicated vCPUs place multi-core throughput in the top twenty-five percent. This configuration fits deep learning model training, molecular modeling, large-scale video processing, and GPU-intensive computational science.
